clue.text: Optical shutter

parts.note: surface reading: a camera part that closes over the lens
setter's reading: the fold of skin that closes over the eye

explanation.walkthrough: 'Optical' pulls toward cameras and lenses, but the shutter meant is part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that blinks down over each eye works like a shutter, cutting off light.

clue.text: Cheer a team endlessly at entry

indicators.note: an entry is a going in, so the small word goes inside the shortened one
without an end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a side of eleven players, as in cricket or football
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fans cheer their side endlessly as it walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: A football or cricket team has eleven players, so a team is named by its number; 'entry' tells the little word to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to lift their spirits, and to elevate is to raise up or uplift.

clue.text: He's paid to say nothing

parts.note: surface reading: someone bribed to keep quiet, hush money
setter's reading: a film actor in a crowd scene with no lines

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests hush money; the person is a background performer with no speaking part.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-speaking background performer in a film or play is employed only to fill the scene, without lines.

clue.text: Suggested one politician was untruthful

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
Member of Parliament
told a falsehood

explanation.surface: It was hinted that a certain politician had been dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied is hinted at indirectly rather than stated outright, so it is suggested.

clue.text: Bail is arranged for those with proofs of innocence

indicators.note: things that are arranged are put into a new order, so the preceding letters are reordered

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A court grants bail to suspects who can show they were elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Each is a claim of having been somewhere else when the crime happened, offered as evidence that clears an accused person.

clue.text: Dismisses a proposal to start moving

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the exhortation 'let us go'

explanation.surface: A boss fires someone and suggests getting a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer who releases staff is said to let them go, and 'let's go' urges a group to set off.

clue.text: Unhappy with split in state of Kentucky?

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
to split or grass is to inform on someone, in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about a division within a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass or split is British slang for informing to the police. 'state' means a nickname, not the state itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Kentucky's nickname is the Bluegrass State, after a meadow grass that thrives on its land.

clue.text: Work for Labour, for example

parts.note: surface reading: campaigning for the British Labour Party
setter's reading: one word that may stand for another of the same meaning

explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes it the political party, but work and labour are simply two words meaning the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another, as work is for labour, is called this in grammar.

clue.text: Dare any health resort claim that all its residents are?

definitions.text: Dare any health resort claim that all its residents are?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning to sort again, so the preceding letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Can a spa honestly boast that every guest is in perfect health?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a spa would like to claim its guests are robust and well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means vigorously healthy, exactly what a spa would hope to say of everyone staying there.

clue.text: Wager about a pound

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a wager wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a bet is a wager
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stakes roughly a pound on an outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pound' reads as a sum of money, but pound here is a verb meaning strike repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat something is to strike it hard and repeatedly, just as one would pound a drum or dough.

clue.text: Fail to honour commitments to one's class?

definitions.text: Fail to honour commitments to one's class?

parts.words: Fail to honour commitments to one's class
parts.note: surface reading: betraying one's social class, as a disloyal aristocrat or worker might
setter's reading: the school class a pupil should be attending

explanation.walkthrough: 'class' suggests social rank and loyalty; it is the schoolroom lesson a pupil skips.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who stays away from school without permission is breaking the obligation to attend lessons.

clue.text: One must back the law to some degree in Africa

definitions.note: the answer is a country in Africa

indicators.note: the word for one must come at the back, placed after everything else

parts.note: Master of Arts, a university degree
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone must support the law, at least partly, somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some degree' sounds like 'partly' but supplies the academic degree; the African country is spelt MA + LAW + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked nation in the south-east of the continent, so it lies within Africa.

clue.text: Taking someone on of attractive disposition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hiring or employing a person

explanation.surface: An employer hiring someone with a pleasant character.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging staff means employing them, and an engaging person has a charming, winning manner.

clue.text: Gazing about

definitions.meaning: second meaning: concerning, on the subject of

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gazing about' reads as looking around; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at attentively, and the preposition regarding means concerning a topic.

clue.text: See lambs going round in flocks together

indicators.note: going round suggests turning and circling, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: the words as printed plus the third S the parse needs and no clue word supplies: the setter's slip

explanation.surface: Watch the lambs circling as they gather in their flocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed fodder rearranges only to ASSEMBLE; the final S of the answer has no source in the clue, a slip by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals or people that gather into a group are coming together, which is what assembling means.

clue.text: Composed a piece of classical music

indicators.note: a piece is only part of the whole, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone wrote a work of classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like the verb for writing music; it is the adjective meaning serene.
explanation.definitionFit: A composed person is serene and untroubled, keeping their cool under pressure.

clue.text: Primate embraces son in church

definitions.note: the answer is a part found in a church

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the first word encloses the next

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A primate, perhaps a senior bishop, hugs a boy during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: A primate is also an archbishop, which suits the church setting, but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar, is an architectural feature found in churches.

clue.text: There's no accounting for his performance

definitions.text: There's no accounting for his performance

parts.words: There's no accounting for his performance
parts.note: surface reading: his acting is baffling and inexplicable
setter's reading: there is no bill or payment for what he does, since he is unpaid

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'no accounting for' means inexplicable; read literally it means no money changes hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who performs or plays for love rather than a fee is a non-professional, unpaid participant.

clue.text: Beneficial, though self-contradictory in parts

parts.note: entire, which clashes with the part that follows
only a portion, the opposite of entire

explanation.surface: Something good for you, though with a few internal inconsistencies.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's two halves mean entire and partial, which contradict each other; that is the joke the clue points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesome food or influence is good for body or mind, so it is beneficial to health.

clue.text: Erudite composer shown the way out

indicators.note: out means on the outside, so the words for shown the way sit outside the composer

parts.note: guided
Thomas Arne, the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A scholarly musician is escorted to the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: ARNE is the crossword's favourite composer. 'the way out' looks like an exit; 'out' alone is the outside signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person has acquired deep knowledge through study, which is what erudite describes.

clue.text: Set off on horseback?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: displayed in a frame or setting, as a picture or gem

explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off on horseback' reads as departing on a ride; 'set off' means displayed to advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo or jewel fixed in a frame is displayed, and a rider sitting on a horse is likewise described this way.

clue.text: Fruit with the top off is still fruit

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, and taking it off removes it

parts.note: a bunch of the yellow fruit

explanation.surface: Even with its top sliced off, a fruit remains a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: BANANAS loses its first letter and leaves the French and botanical name for the pineapple.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is another name for the pineapple, a tropical fruit, used in French and in botany.

clue.text: It's a man found shipwrecked on a Pacific island

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken up and scattered, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken letter for letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A castaway is discovered after a shipwreck on a remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' before the definition joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the large island state south of mainland Australia, on the edge of the Pacific region.

clue.text: King for half a year and one short day

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only one of its two halves, dropping the other

parts.note: taken as written; only its second half is kept

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the day's name loses its end

parts.note: Thursday in its usual short form, then trimmed further
one particular day of the week

explanation.surface: A monarch whose reign lasted half a year and a day.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of YEAR is AR; THURS loses its last letter to give THUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur is the legendary British king of Camelot and the Round Table.

clue.text: Boy, it rises — and falls!

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading upward, so the words are taken from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at something going up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: something that rises and falls is like the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal water rises and falls twice daily with the tides, which is exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: General still a duke, even if losing his head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British commander who defeated Napoleon at Waterloo

definitions.text: still a duke, even if losing his head
definitions.note: a cryptic description: without its first letter the name is still a Duke
definitions.meaning: second meaning: he was a duke, and his name minus its first letter is the jazz bandleader Duke Ellington

explanation.surface: A general remains a nobleman even if beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington was made Duke of Wellington; drop the W and Ellington remains, the jazz composer known as Duke Ellington.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Wellesley, the first Duke of Wellington, was the British general who won at Waterloo.

clue.text: Tax office

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a levy, as on imports
second meaning: a role or obligation one must perform

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax office' looks like a government building; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy charged on goods is a customs duty, and one's office or job carries obligations called duties.

clue.text: Is among those left to fight

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the first word goes inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the rest are those who remain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joins the remaining few to keep up the struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or struggle against an attacker or pressure, which is to fight it.

clue.text: Rotten theologian in crooked deal

indicators.note: in places the theologian inside the reworked letters
crooked means bent out of shape, so the following word's letters are twisted around

parts.note: taken letter for letter, to be reworked
Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: A corrupt cleric is caught up in a dishonest transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled eggs have gone bad, so addled means rotten as well as muddled.
